briefs.topic: Intergroup tension as a quantified unrest hazard: a tension-index stock, its immigration-rate x economic-stress x segregation inflow, decay constants, and an unrest-hazard multiplier for the 2026-2036 demography layer
key_numbers: Austerity->unrest (Ponticelli & Voth, Europe 1919-2008, ~26 countries): expenditure cuts of 0-2% GDP sit near baseline unrest frequency; 2-5% cuts roughly double the count of CHAOS unrest events (riots+demonstrations+strikes+assassinations+attempted revolutions); >5% cuts triple-plus it. Every +1pp of GDP in cuts raises the unrest index materially; TAX rises have only small effects (asymmetry: spending cuts are the potent lever). Constraints-on-executive attenuate the effect.

Economic-shock->conflict elasticity (Miguel, Satyanath & Sergenti, 41 African countries 1981-99, rainfall-IV): a NEGATIVE growth shock of 5pp raises conflict probability the following year by ~half its baseline (~an 8pp rise on a ~27% base). Not significantly larger in more ethnically diverse countries -> economic stress dominates over composition as a trigger.

Unrest persistence & contagion (Barrett et al., IMF Reported Social Unrest Index, 130 countries, 1985-present): a major unrest event QUADRUPLES the probability of another within 6 months in the same country and DOUBLES it in a neighbor. In level terms: ~+3pp own-country and ~+1pp neighbor unrest probability over the next 6 months. This is the empirical basis for a self-exciting (Hawkes-like) inflow term.

Macro cost of unrest (Hadzi-Vaskov, Pienknagura & Ricci, IMF WP/23/232): a one-standard-deviation rise in the unrest index leaves GDP ~0.2pp below baseline 6 quarters out; a major unrest EVENT (large index jump) is associated with ~1.0pp lower GDP after 6 quarters, driven by manufacturing, services and consumption contractions. Effects partially mean-revert.

Immigration RATE (not level) drives hostility & hate crime: Entorf & Lange (Germany 2014-15 quasi-random asylum allocation) find anti-refugee hate crime concentrates where a LARGE inflow hits regions with LOW prior foreign-born share -> the interaction (inflow rate x low prior exposure) is the driver, not the stock level. Hangartner et al. (2019 APSR, Greek islands natural experiment): sudden refugee exposure caused large, persistent (~1yr) increases in native hostility even though refugees only transited -> pure rate/exposure shock, not economic or contact channel.

Compositional shock -> far-right vote (electoral analog of tension): Dinas et al. (Golden Dawn, Aegean islands): sudden refugee exposure raised Golden Dawn vote ~+2pp (~+44% at the mean). Hopkins 'Politicized Places': sudden local immigrant-share CHANGE provokes opposition ONLY when national salience is high; absent national rhetoric, changing vs static counties differ by ~0.1pp -> rate effect is CONDITIONAL on national salience.

Immigration<->crime elasticity is small/near-zero: total-crime elasticity to refugee inflow ~0.05 (some estimates 0.16 UK asylum / Germany refugees; ~0.39 for one former-Soviet-origin flow). 215-region European panel finds no causal immigration->crime link. Tension is a perception/threat channel, largely decoupled from actual crime rates.

Contact vs threat (Pettigrew & Tropp meta-analysis, 515 studies / 713 samples / >250k subjects): intergroup contact reduces prejudice, mean r=-0.21; Allport's optimal conditions (equal status, common goals, cooperation, institutional support) amplify but are not necessary. Threat/'halo effect' is the counterforce: far-right support peaks at INTERMEDIATE distance from diverse areas (proximity without contact) -> segregation is the switch between contact (decay) and threat (inflow).

Diversity->trust is CONTESTED and small when it exists (Dinesen, Schaeffer & Sonderskov 2020 meta-analysis, 1,001 estimates / 87 studies; van der Meer & Tolsma review, 90 studies): the negative diversity-trust association is (a) robust mainly for NEIGHBORHOOD-level, spatially-bounded cohesion, (b) stronger in the US than Europe, (c) about out-group SIZE/segregation not interethnic trust per se, and (d) attenuates or vanishes with controls for deprivation and segregation. Effect sizes are small; residential segregation, not diversity per se, mediates.

Riot magnitudes for calibration: 1919 (Chicago/Red Summer) and 1965-68 US waves -> Collins & Margo: severe-riot cities saw ~9% relative decline in median black family income and lasting black-owned property-value depression through the 1970s. 1992 LA riots: >50 deaths, ~2,300 injured, ~1,100 buildings damaged, ~$1bn property damage. DiPasquale & Glaeser: ethnic diversity and non-white YOUNG-MALE unemployment (opportunity cost of time), not poverty per se, predict riot incidence/intensity.

Recent European episode costs/durations: 2005 French riots ~3 weeks, ~10,000 cars burned, ~EUR204m damage; 2023 Nahel/France riots ~1 week but ~EUR650m insured damage (more intense, shorter); 2024 UK (Southport) far-right riots across ~27 towns, ~1,280 arrests, ~GBP31.7m policing cost, concentrated in high-deprivation towns with the largest post-2010 local-service budget cuts -> confirms deprivation x compositional-grievance x national salience interaction.
base_rates: Baseline (no austerity, no compositional shock) European CHAOS unrest frequency is low-single-digit events per country-decade; the count roughly doubles in the 2-5% GDP-cut band and triples above 5% (Ponticelli & Voth). Use ~1-2 'unrest-relevant' events/country-decade as the quiescent base, scaled by the hazard multiplier below.

Conditional on one major unrest event, P(another within 6 months) ~ 4x baseline own-country, ~2x in a neighbor (Barrett/IMF). Translates to a self-excitation decay half-life of ~3-6 months on the acute component of the tension index.

A 5pp negative growth shock ~ +50% relative rise in conflict onset probability the following year (Miguel et al.); treat economic stress as the single largest multiplicative trigger, larger than composition alone.

Sudden-inflow-driven far-right/hostility surges run ~+2pp vote (+40-45% relative) per major local exposure shock (Dinas et al.), but only when national salience is high (Hopkins) -> gate the compositional inflow on a national-salience term already present in your sentiment/election mechanics.

Macro cost per major unrest event ~ -1pp GDP at 6 quarters, ~-0.2pp per 1-SD index rise (IMF), partially reverting -> matches your existing unrest_gdp_cost level effect (currently 0.01*unrest); calibrate the coefficient so a saturated tension-driven unrest episode costs ~1pp GDP.
Contact effect size r~-0.21 (Pettigrew & Tropp) sets the maximum decay rate achievable through integration/contact; segregation near 1 suppresses this to ~0, near 0 realizes it fully.
contested: Whether ethnic DIVERSITY per se erodes social trust/cohesion is genuinely disputed: Dinesen-Schaeffer-Sonderskov (2020) and van der Meer-Tolsma find the negative association is small, largely confined to neighborhood-level spatially-bounded cohesion, stronger in the US than Europe, and often attenuates to null once segregation and deprivation are controlled. Do NOT hard-code a diversity->trust penalty; model segregation and inflow-rate as the drivers and treat the level of diversity as near-neutral.

Level vs rate-of-change vs segregation as the operative variable is contested: the strongest quasi-experimental evidence (Entorf-Lange, Hangartner et al., Dinas et al., Hopkins) favors RATE-of-change x low-prior-exposure x national-salience over static level; but Putnam-tradition and 'halo effect' work emphasize segregation/composition (a level-and-spatial-structure story). The model should carry both an acute rate-driven inflow and a slower segregation-mediated term, not collapse them.

Whether austerity's unrest effect is truly separate from the business cycle: Ponticelli-Voth argue spending cuts matter beyond GDP downturns (and tax rises don't), but re-analyses of the economic-shock->conflict literature (Miguel et al. vs its published comments, e.g. the AEJ 'Re-examining' exchange) show the growth-conflict elasticity is sensitive to specification and sample. Treat the economic-stress multiplier as a plausible-range parameter, not a point estimate.

Contact-hypothesis external validity is contested: meta-analytic r~-0.21 is robust in-sample, but field/'re-evaluated' critiques (contact often correlates with self-selection; effects shrink in real segregated settings and for majority groups). Realized decay from contact should be gated hard by segregation and should not be assumed to operate at scale under residential separation.

Immigration->crime is largely a NULL result in the causal literature (near-zero elasticities, no-link European panels); tension must therefore be modeled as a perceived-threat channel, keyed to salience and inflow rate, explicitly decoupled from any actual-crime stock. Coding tension as if it tracked real crime would contradict the evidence.

stocks: tension_index (T): 0..1 latent intergroup-tension stock, analogous to and feeding the existing society `unrest` stock. Split into two coupled components for correct dynamics: T_acute (fast, self-exciting, 0..1) and T_structural (slow, segregation-and-grievance-fed baseline, 0..1); T = clamp(T_structural + T_acute, 0, 1).

segregation_index (Seg): 0..1 slow-moving residential/social separation stock; the SWITCH variable that routes composition into either the contact decay channel (Seg low) or the threat inflow channel (Seg high). Fed by immigration settlement pattern and solidarity_index from the demography layer.
salience (Sal): reuse the existing S1 sentiment / national-rhetoric term (0..1) as a GATE, not a new stock -- Hopkins/Dinas show compositional inflow only bites when national salience is high.
flows: INFLOW_acute = k_in * f(imm_rate) * g(econ_stress) * h(Seg) * Sal, where imm_rate is the immigration FLOW (rate of change of foreign-born share, from the immigration valve), NOT the level. Suggested forms: f(imm_rate)=imm_rate normalized so a 'sudden large inflow into low-prior-exposure region' saturates (interaction with low prior exposure per Entorf-Lange); g(econ_stress)=(1 + beta_e*max(0, -growth_shock/5pp)) capturing the Miguel 5pp->~+50% elasticity and the Ponticelli-Voth austerity asymmetry (spending-cut term weighted ~3-5x any tax term); h(Seg)=Seg (threat channel scales with segregation). k_in calibrated so one major exposure shock in a high-salience, high-segregation, recession year moves T_acute by ~0.15-0.25.

SELF_EXCITATION = lambda_self * T_acute * (1 - T_acute): Hawkes-style term encoding Barrett's 4x-within-6-months persistence; plus optional neighbor/contagion coupling at ~half strength (2x) if multiple regions are modeled.
DECAY_acute = T_acute / tau_acute: exponential relaxation of the fast component. tau_acute ~ 0.4-0.6 yr (half-life ~3-5 months) to reproduce the 6-month persistence window.

DECAY_structural (contact channel) = c_contact * (1 - Seg) * T_structural, magnitude capped by the contact effect size (r~-0.21 sets the ceiling); realized only when segregation is low. When Seg high, structural decay -> ~0 and T_structural persists.

STRUCTURAL_BUILD = k_struct * Seg * (1 - solidarity_index) * unremediated_grievance: slow accretion of baseline tension from segregation + eroded solidarity + the existing grievance stock; tau_structural ~ 3-6 yr.
couplings: tension_index -> society.unrest: T raises the unrest boil hazard. Concretely, make the existing unrest boil condition (grievance unremediated AND inst_trust<0.35) fire probabilistically via an unrest-hazard MULTIPLIER M(T, econ_stress) (see lessons) rather than a hard threshold; T also raises the steady-state unrest level. Keep unrest's existing consequences (adoption x0.75 / the 1-0.25*unrest term, and unrest_gdp_cost).

econ_stress <- macro layer (growth shock, austerity/transfer stress): shared input to both INFLOW_acute (trigger) and to the unrest GDP-cost channel; a negative growth shock both raises tension inflow and deepens the GDP hit (feedback with displacement).

solidarity_index (demography) -> STRUCTURAL_BUILD and -> transfers gate: low solidarity feeds structural tension AND (per the demography design) throttles transfers, which raises unremediated_grievance -> a reinforcing loop the model should expose as a leverage point.

immigration valve -> imm_rate (INFLOW_acute) and -> Seg settlement: the flow enters tension via its RATE and via how it changes segregation; the level of foreign-born share is deliberately near-neutral (contested diversity-trust literature).

salience (S1 sentiment/election rhetoric) -> gates INFLOW_acute: closes the tension->unrest channel in low-salience regimes and opens it in high-salience election years, linking to your election mechanics.
tension_index -> GDP (via unrest): calibrate so a saturated tension-driven unrest episode costs ~1pp GDP at ~6 quarters, matching IMF, partially mean-reverting as T_acute decays.

lessons_for_model: Model the tension INFLOW as a MULTIPLICATIVE interaction of immigration-RATE x economic-stress x segregation, gated by national salience -- not additive, and not keyed to the immigration LEVEL. The quasi-experimental evidence (Entorf-Lange, Hangartner, Dinas, Hopkins) is specifically about sudden inflow into low-prior-exposure, high-salience contexts. A pure-level or pure-diversity driver would contradict the contested trust literature.

Concrete unrest-hazard multiplier: M(T, s) = 1 + a*T + b*max(0, -growth_shock/0.05) + c*T*max(0,-growth_shock/0.05), with the INTERACTION term c dominant (economic downturn x compositional tension is where riots cluster). Suggested starting values a~1.5, b~1.0 (from Miguel 5pp->~+50%), c~2.0; then apply Ponticelli-Voth austerity asymmetry by feeding spending-cut stress into growth_shock at ~3-5x the weight of tax stress. M multiplies the baseline unrest boil hazard (a Poisson/logistic rate), replacing the current hard threshold with hazard = base_rate * M, so unrest becomes probabilistic and can self-excite.

Give tension TWO time constants: a fast self-exciting acute component (tau_acute ~ 0.4-0.6 yr, half-life 3-5 months, lambda_self tuned to Barrett's 4x-in-6-months) and a slow structural component (tau_structural ~ 3-6 yr) fed by segregation and eroded solidarity. Riots are bursty and mean-reverting (2005/2023 France, 2024 UK lasted days-to-weeks) but the baseline they revert to drifts with segregation. A single decay constant cannot reproduce both.

Make segregation the SWITCH between contact (decay) and threat (inflow): realized prejudice-decay is capped at the Pettigrew-Tropp r~-0.21 ceiling and scales with (1-Seg); the threat/halo inflow scales with Seg. This lets integration policy / desegregation act as a genuine Meadows leverage point (flip the sign of the composition->tension channel) rather than a marginal parameter tweak.

Decouple tension from actual crime: the immigration->crime elasticity is ~0-0.16 (mostly null in causal European panels). Tension is a perceived-threat/salience channel. Do not let a crime stock drive tension; drive it from inflow rate, economic stress, segregation and national rhetoric.

Calibrate consequences to IMF magnitudes: a major tension-driven unrest event should cost ~1pp GDP at ~6 quarters (0.2pp per 1-SD), partially reverting -- consistent with the existing unrest_gdp_cost=0.01*unrest level effect. Keep unrest's throttle on adoption (the 1-0.25*unrest term) since trust collapse must not read as pro-adoption.

Flag three literatures as CONTESTED in code comments and expose them as sensitivity parameters, not point estimates: (1) diversity->trust (small, US>Europe, neighborhood-bounded, segregation-mediated, often null with controls); (2) rate vs level vs segregation as operative variable (carry both acute-rate and structural-segregation terms); (3) austerity-vs-cycle separability and the growth-conflict elasticity's specification-sensitivity. Ship each as a low/central/high range so the red-team can stress it.

Encode the reinforcing loop explicitly as a leverage point: low solidarity_index -> throttled transfers -> higher unremediated grievance -> higher structural tension -> more unrest -> lower solidarity. This R-loop, gated by salience, is where the demography and society layers couple; the intervention points are the transfers gate (solidarity threshold) and the segregation switch (contact channel).

briefs.topic: Grievance redirection (scapegoating) dynamics: how economic-anxiety backlash from automation/trade gets routed onto outgroups instead of the causal technology/firms; restriction as a policy relief valve substituting for transfers; couplings for the 2026-2036 AI-transition systems model
key_numbers: Trade shock -> nativist vote (US): Autor-Dorn-Hanson-Majlesi (AER 2020, 'Importing Political Polarization') — rising Chinese import penetration causally increased county GOP presidential two-party vote share 2000-16 and removed moderates from Congress; counterfactual with 50%-lower import-penetration growth flips MI/WI/PA to Clinton in 2016. Note the backlash landed on TRADE/IMMIGRATION platforms, not on automating firms. https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.20170011

Trade shock -> nativist vote (EU): Colantone & Stanig (AJPS 2018), 15 W. European countries 1988-2007 — 1 SD increase in regional Chinese-import shock raises radical-right vote share by roughly 0.7pp at district level (baseline radical-right shares typically 5-10%), plus a general rightward/nationalist shift. https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/ajps.12358

Robot shock -> radical right (EU): Anelli-Colantone-Stanig (PNAS 2021) — moving from 25th to 75th percentile of individual robot-exposure raises radical-right vote probability by +3.5pp against a sample mean of ~5% (a ~70% relative increase); mechanism runs through perceived economic decline, lower government/democracy satisfaction, lower political self-efficacy. https://www.pnas.org/doi/10.1073/pnas.2111611118

Robot shock -> Trump 2016: Frey-Berger-Chen (Oxford Rev Econ Policy 2018) — had robot exposure not increased in the years before 2016, MI, PA, and WI would have swung to Clinton, flipping the Electoral College. Automation grievance was harvested by an anti-trade/anti-immigrant platform, not an anti-automation one. https://academic.oup.com/oxrep/article-abstract/34/3/418/5047377

MISATTRIBUTION CORE RESULT: Wu (PSRM 2022, 'Misattributed blame?') — using ANES 2016, workers at higher automation risk are significantly more likely to oppose free trade and favor immigration restriction, controlling for standard determinants, while NOT punishing technology; automation threat intensifies anti-globalization demands. Direct evidence that structural-cause grievance is routed to trade/outgroups. https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/political-science-research-and-methods/article/misattributed-blame-attitudes-toward-globalization-in-the-age-of-automation/29B08295CEAC4A4A89991E064D0284FF

Attribution gap 2025-26 (US): Gallup/SCSP — 42% name 'AI taking jobs' as the top AI danger and 97% want AI safety rules, yet only ~1% of laid-off workers cite AI/automation as the primary reason for their own job cut, and AI does not register at all on Gallup's Most Important Problem list through mid-2026; immigration by contrast hit a record 28% MIP (Feb 2024) and still ~20% (Feb 2026). Salience ratio outgroup:AI-cause on the order of 20:1 despite AI being the named anxiety. https://news.gallup.com/poll/694685/americans-prioritize-safety-data-security.aspx ; https://news.gallup.com/poll/611135/immigration-surges-top-important-problem-list.aspx

Refugee exposure -> far-right vote: Dinas-Matakos-Xefteris-Hangartner (Political Analysis 2019) — Greek islands receiving sudden Syrian refugee flows in 2015 saw Golden Dawn vote rise ~+2pp (+44% relative). Dustmann-Vasiljeva-Damm (ReStud 2019, Denmark quasi-random allocation): +1pp refugee share -> +1.34pp anti-immigration-party vote in non-urban municipalities; SIGN FLIPS (negative) in the most urban municipalities — supports your exposure-heterogeneity design. https://academic.oup.com/restud/article-abstract/86/5/2035/5112970

Outgroup salience -> transfer shrink: Alesina-Miano-Stantcheva (ReStud 2023, 6 countries) — respondents overestimate immigrant shares ~2x and immigrant unemployment by 21-30pp; merely priming immigration before redistribution questions causally REDUCES stated support for redistribution and real charitable giving; perceived immigrant free-riding is the strongest single correlate of low redistribution support (stronger than cultural distance). Dahlberg-Edmark-Lundqvist (JPE 2012, Swedish quasi-random refugee placement): larger immigrant share -> lower preferred benefit levels, concentrated among high-income natives. https://academic.oup.com/restud/article-abstract/90/1/1/6547062

Historical restriction-with-retrenchment: Tabellini (ReStud 2020, US cities 1910-30) — immigration triggered election of more conservative legislators, support for the 1920s Immigration Acts, and CUTS to tax rates and public spending (education, sanitation), despite no measurable native wage/employment losses; i.e., backlash produced restriction PLUS smaller government, not compensation. https://academic.oup.com/restud/article/87/1/454/5486071

Relief valve delivers no relief: Lee-Peri-Yasenov (J Public Econ 2022) — 1930s repatriation of ~400,000 Mexicans produced ZERO native employment gains; causal estimates show null-to-negative effects on native employment and wages plus occupational downgrading of incumbents. Restriction reduced political salience but not the underlying grievance. https://www.nber.org/papers/w26399

1930s scapegoating base rates: Nazi vote in industrial Saxony 4.9% (1928) -> 43.7% (1932) tracking unemployment; Galofre-Vila et al. (NBER w24106) — localities with larger austerity (spending cuts + tax rises) had higher Nazi vote share in every federal election 1930-33; Doerr-Gissler-Peydro-Voth (CEPR) — the 1931 Danatbank failure (Jewish-chaired) raised antisemitic persecution most where locals were exposed to it: scapegoating amplifies where a visible 'damning' outgroup narrative exists. https://cepr.org/voxeu/columns/fiscal-austerity-and-rise-nazis

Media framing elasticity: Djourelova (AER 2023) — AP's 2013 ban on 'illegal immigrant' cut the term's use 28% in AP-reliant outlets; 1 SD greater exposure to the language change -> -0.8pp support for restrictive border policy (~2% of the R-D partisan gap), moderates most affected. A single-phrase supply-side framing shift moves restriction preferences by measurable amounts. https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257/aer.20211537

Framing supply side: Hameleers-Bos-de Vreese (Communication Research 2017) and 15-16 country experiments — explicit blame-attribution messages causally shift blame perceptions and populist attitudes, but only among recipients who identify with the source; counter-identified recipients move the OPPOSITE way. Blame routing is elite-supplied and identity-gated, not automatic. https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/0093650216644026

Radical right in government: Chueri (Party Politics 2021; Scand Pol Studies 2022) — radical-right government participation produces welfare DUALIZATION (chauvinism): retrenchment targeted at 'undeserving' groups (immigrants, unemployed) with maintained or expanded benefits for 'deserving' natives (pensions) — not across-the-board retrenchment. https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1177/1354068820923496
base_rates: Share of automation/trade-driven economic-anxiety backlash landing on outgroups/trade vs on the causal technology/firms: no single published split exists, but triangulation (Wu 2022 misattribution; ADH-Majlesi and Frey harvesting by nativist platforms; Gallup 42% AI-job-anxiety vs ~1% own-layoff attribution and zero MIP salience vs immigration 20-28%) supports a historical routing of roughly 70-85% of realized political energy onto outgroups/trade/elites and only ~15-30% onto the technology/firms/policy actually responsible. Use 0.75 baseline redirect_share for 2026-29, declining toward 0.5-0.6 by 2032-36 as AI becomes a named, branded, visible cause (unlike diffuse 'automation') — the robot era had near-total redirect; AI already polls at 42% named anxiety, so redirect should be lower than the 1990s-2016 base rate.

Nativist-vote elasticity to economic shock: ~0.7pp radical-right vote per 1 SD trade shock (EU districts); +3.5pp per interquartile robot-exposure move (individual, vs 5% base). Treat ~0.5-1pp per 1 SD displacement shock as the district-level base rate for the outgroup-directed channel.

Anti-immigration vote per unit local exposure: +1.34pp per +1pp refugee population share (non-urban); ~0 to negative in dense urban areas. Golden Dawn: +2pp (+44% relative) from transient high-visibility exposure even WITHOUT labor-market competition — visibility, not economics, drives the local trigger.

Restriction-episode hazard conditional on (economic distress spike AND migration salience spike): historically near-deterministic within 3-5 years — 1921/1924 US Quota Acts after WWI recession + Red Scare; 1929-34 repatriations in the Depression; 2016-18 EU asylum tightening after 2015 crisis + post-2008 wage stagnation; 2025-26 US enforcement surge after the 2023-24 border salience peak. Model annual restriction hazard rising from ~5-10% baseline to 40-60%/yr when unrest stock is boiling AND immigration salience >20% MIP-equivalent.

Relief-valve effectiveness: restriction reliably cuts SALIENCE (US immigration MIP fell from 28% peak toward and below 20% during 2025-26 enforcement) but delivers ~zero measured wage/employment relief to natives (Lee-Peri-Yasenov 1930s: null-to-negative; Tabellini 1910-30: no native gains from immigrant losses). So grievance decays only via the sentiment channel, not the income channel, and re-accumulates with continued displacement.

Transfer-shrink from outgroup salience: priming immigration measurably reduces redistribution support (Alesina et al., significant on stated preferences AND real donations); exogenous refugee inflow reduced preferred benefit levels especially among high-income voters (Dahlberg et al.); 1910-30 US immigration lowered per-capita public spending and tax rates. A reasonable parameterization: each sustained 1 SD rise in outgroup salience shaves 3-8% off transfer generosity growth or delays expansion by roughly one electoral cycle.

Media/elite framing leverage on the routing split: a single wire-service language change moved restriction preferences 0.8pp per 1 SD exposure (~2% of the partisan gap); blame-frame experiments move blame perceptions significantly but only among source-identifiers. Framing shifts plausibly move redirect_share by +/-0.1-0.2, not by 0.5 — elite framing tilts, it does not reverse.
contested: Economic vs cultural roots of nativist backlash: Autor et al., Colantone-Stanig, Anelli et al. establish causal LOCAL effects of economic shocks on nativist voting, but Margalit (JEP 2019) argues economic insecurity explains only a MODEST share of total populist support (important 'on the margin', decisive in close elections, not the main level) and that immigration concern is only marginally economic; a 2024 SSRN critique (Kaestner) disputes attributing ADH effects to China specifically. Model implication: keep the displacement->sentiment elasticity real but modest, with the margin mattering via your election mechanics, not as the sole driver of nativist stock.

Do transfers/compensation attenuate the backlash? CONTESTED BOTH WAYS. Pro-attenuation: austerity literatures (Galofre-Vila et al. Nazi vote; Fetzer's Brexit-austerity work) show benefit CUTS causally fuel radical votes, implying transfers suppress them. Anti-attenuation: Gingrich finds cross-national differences in compensation strategy had LIMITED direct or indirect effect on how the automation-exposed voted; Spanish survey experiments find automation threat does NOT raise demand for redistribution relative to trade threat, nor stronger deservingness beliefs. Recommended: transfer->unrest attenuation with wide uncertainty band (e.g., multiplier 0.5-0.9 on grievance accrual), and do NOT assume transfers redirect blame back onto AI firms.

Does restriction SUBSTITUTE for or COMPLEMENT welfare expansion? Substitution evidence: Tabellini (restriction era came with tax and spending CUTS); Alesina et al./Dahlberg et al. (outgroup salience shrinks the redistribution coalition); Chueri (radical-right incumbency -> dualization, retrenchment for 'undeserving'). Complement evidence: Danish Social Democrats explicitly paired hardline restriction WITH leftward welfare moves, arguing restriction preserves fiscal room and solidarity for universal transfers ('a welfare state cannot afford liberal immigration'); welfare-chauvinist parties defend generous native benefits. Both are published positions; the literature does not adjudicate cleanly. Model as regime-dependent: restriction under nativist-right coalitions shrinks/delays transfers; restriction under center-left 'Danish model' coalitions protects or slightly expands native transfers.

Contact vs threat: local outgroup exposure INCREASES anti-immigration voting in rural/low-density areas (Dustmann +1.34pp; Dinas +2pp) but DECREASES or nulls it in dense urban areas — the halo/contact dispute is genuinely unresolved in aggregate; your exposure-heterogeneity design should carry the sign flip rather than a single elasticity.

Whether AI-specific backlash will follow the robot-era redirect pattern: the CFR 'Coming AI Backlash' and 2025-26 polling (bipartisan 97% wanting rules, hard negative sentiment shift) suggest AI firms may be a far more nameable target than 1990s-2010s automation; but Gallup MIP shows zero realized salience through mid-2026. Extrapolation of redirect_share decline is a modeling judgment, not a published finding — flag it as such.

stocks: Grievance (existing unrest-stock input): unremediated displacement grievance, accruing from displacement rate minus remediation (transfers) and minus salience-decay from relief-valve policies

BlamePool routed into two sub-stocks by redirect_share: Blame_Outgroup (nativist pressure) and Blame_AIFirms (regulatory/backlash pressure on adoption) — conserved flow: energy sent to one is unavailable to the other
ImmigrationSalience (MIP-style 0-1 index): driven by Blame_Outgroup, media/elite framing, and local exposure heterogeneity; decays after restriction acts (observed 28%->20% US 2024-26)
SolidarityIndex (existing demography-layer stock): eroded by ImmigrationSalience (Alesina priming, Dahlberg), gates transfer expansion
RestrictionPolicyLevel: ratchet-like stock raised by restriction hazard events; feeds back to close the demography layer's immigration flow valve
TransferGenerosity: expanded by grievance + pro-transfer coalition, shrunk/delayed by low SolidarityIndex and by nativist-right incumbency (regime switch)
flows: blame_routing: d(Blame_Outgroup)/dt = redirect_share x grievance_expression_rate; d(Blame_AIFirms)/dt = (1 - redirect_share) x grievance_expression_rate. redirect_share_0 = 0.75 (2026), drifting to ~0.55 by 2034 as AI visibility rises; modified +/-0.15 by elite_framing parameter and by whether displacement events are publicly attributed to AI (Gallup attribution gap closing)

restriction_hazard: logistic in (ImmigrationSalience x unrest_boiling flag x election proximity); 5-10%/yr baseline -> 40-60%/yr in joint-spike states; firing raises RestrictionPolicyLevel, cuts immigration inflow valve 30-70%, and decays ImmigrationSalience with ~1-2yr half-life

relief_valve_null_relief: restriction events give NO income-channel grievance relief (Lee-Peri-Yasenov) — only the salience/sentiment channel decays; grievance re-accumulates at the ongoing displacement rate, so the valve buys 2-4 years then re-pressurizes

transfer_expansion: gated by SolidarityIndex threshold; each sustained 1 SD of ImmigrationSalience applies 0.92-0.97 multiplier to transfer growth or one-electoral-cycle delay; under nativist-right regimes apply dualization (native-targeted transfers maintained, universal/outgroup transfers cut)
solidarity_erosion: dSolidarity/dt negative in ImmigrationSalience with the misperception amplifier (perceived immigrant share ~2x actual)
couplings: tension -> B2 backlash attenuation on AI adoption: effective_adoption_throttle = base_throttle x (1 + k x Blame_AIFirms) where only the (1 - redirect_share) fraction of boiling unrest feeds Blame_AIFirms. With redirect_share=0.75, the existing x0.75 adoption throttle should weaken to roughly x0.92-0.94 during scapegoating episodes — the counterintuitive result: HIGH nativist tension PROTECTS AI adoption by absorbing the backlash energy. Only when redirect_share falls (AI nameability up, elite framing turns on firms) does the full x0.75 throttle bind

tension -> transfer delay/shrink: TransferGenerosity growth x (1 - 0.03..0.08 x salience_SD), plus regime switch: nativist-right election victory (probability raised ~0.5-1pp per 1 SD displacement shock via your election mechanics, using the 0.7pp/SD and +3.5pp interquartile base rates) triggers dualization: -10-20% on outgroup-accessible transfers, 0 to +5% on native-targeted transfers (Chueri). Reinforcing trap R-loop: displacement -> salience -> solidarity erosion -> fewer transfers -> more unremediated grievance -> more salience

tension -> restriction policy hazard: hazard(t) = base x exp(a x ImmigrationSalience + b x unrest_boiling + c x election_year); calibrate so joint distress+salience spikes fire restriction within 3-5 years with ~near-certainty (4/4 historical episodes). Restriction then couples BACK to: (i) demography immigration valve (close 30-70%), (ii) ImmigrationSalience decay (relief valve), (iii) NO grievance income relief, (iv) labor-supply/wage-inflation channel in the macro layer, and (v) under nativist regimes, transfer dualization above

lessons_for_model: Model blame as a CONSERVED routed flow, not independent stocks: every unit of backlash energy redirected onto migrants is a unit NOT applied to AI firms. This is the load-bearing counterintuitive coupling — historical redirect_share of ~0.7-0.85 means the society layer's B2 adoption throttle should rarely bind at full strength in the 2026-2030 window, because the nativist channel (parties, media infrastructure, 20% standing MIP salience) is already built while AI has zero MIP salience despite 42% named anxiety.

Make redirect_share endogenous to three published determinants: (1) cause visibility/nameability — AI is a branded villain in a way diffuse 'automation' never was, so drift redirect_share down over the decade; (2) elite framing supply — movable by +/-0.1-0.2, identity-gated (Hameleers: frames only persuade in-group identifiers; Djourelova: 1 SD media-language exposure moves policy preferences 0.8pp); (3) local outgroup visibility with your urban/rural sign flip (Dustmann).

Restriction is a relief valve that vents SALIENCE, not GRIEVANCE: it reliably fires (near-deterministic 3-5yr hazard after joint distress+salience spikes), reliably cools measured salience (US 2024-26), delivers zero income relief (1930s repatriation null/negative results), and closes your demography immigration valve — so the model should show restriction buying 2-4 years of apparent calm while the grievance stock keeps filling and labor supply shrinks.

The transfer coupling is a reinforcing trap, not a balancing loop: displacement raises outgroup salience, salience erodes the solidarity index, low solidarity gates transfers shut, absent transfers leave grievance unremediated, feeding salience. Alesina/Dahlberg/Tabellini all show the shrink direction causally; only the Danish regime (restriction-as-complement under center-left) breaks the trap — worth a regime-switch parameter rather than a universal elasticity.

Do not let transfers automatically redirect blame onto AI firms or automatically suppress backlash: the compensation-attenuation literature is genuinely split (austerity clearly fuels radical votes; but Gingrich finds compensation differences barely moved automation-exposed voters, and automation threat does not even raise redistribution demand relative to trade threat). Use a wide band (0.5-0.9 attenuation multiplier) and mark it as a key sensitivity.

Election mechanics hookup: use ~0.5-1pp nativist vote share per 1 SD displacement shock (district level) and +1.34pp per 1pp visible-outgroup share in low-density regions as the two additive channels; economic channel is 'important on the margin' (Margalit) — decisive in close elections via your existing election module, not a wholesale realignment driver.

For the 2030s half of the run: as AI displacement becomes publicly attributed (attribution gap closing from today's ~20:1), redirect_share falls, Blame_AIFirms accumulates, and the model should endogenously produce the delayed-but-sharper AI regulation/backlash scenario — pressure on AI firms arrives LATE precisely because scapegoating absorbed the early wave; that lag is the historically grounded prediction.
